blocks.content: Optional awareness of safe behavior around running aircraft/rotor systems.

items.definition: Around a running helicopter: (1) stay clear of the tail rotor at all times, (2) approach only from the front within the pilot's field of view, (3) never approach until the pilot signals it is safe.
items.analogy: Like approaching a running industrial fan — you never walk around the back where you can't see the blades clearly, and you always wait for someone to signal it's safe.

blocks.question: When approaching a running helicopter on the ramp, what is the correct practice?
choices: Stay clear of the tail rotor, approach from the front, and wait for the pilot's signal
Approach from the rear where ground wash is least, staying low
Approach from either side — the main rotor is the only real hazard
Approach only after the engine is at idle power regardless of pilot signal
blocks.feedback: The tail rotor is nearly invisible when spinning and is a lethal hazard. You must approach from the front where the pilot can see you, and only after receiving the go-ahead signal.
